translated_text: 5. 1.38 Babies, your letter finally arrived last night. I just can't understand why we didn't get any mail for so long. Besides, I always wrote immediately when I knew something definite. Little one, I won't complain anymore, and Tape, but if this keeps going on, I'll be ready for a sanatorium. It's a shame that so much valuable energy is wasted. The three-day journey didn't bother me at all. But ayod, I still need three visas: Hungary, Yugoslavia, and Switzerland. The Yugoslavian one was submitted yesterday. I have to submit it in Belgrade, and that takes days. In my desperation, I contacted the Foreign Ministry again. Dr. From returned today, I was told. I went there immediately, spoke with his representative, arranged a follow-up call, and now I'm sitting downstairs in the Foreign Ministry waiting for the letter they'll give me for the National Bank. So I'm going to try one more time to get the plane ticket approved. Gabriel, you'll only be able to grasp all of this when I tell you everything in person. It couldn't be more complicated. What you know is at most 10% of it. I'm doing my best. Sometimes things just fail me so easily. But my nerves are simply frayed. Do you know how happy I would be if I had all this behind me already?!!! You can be sure that I'm doing everything I can. Of course, I've made mistakes too; but if one knew everything beforehand, in person... Regarding the telegram I sent, it has naturally become obsolete due to the letter about my visit to Tron today. Little one, please don't be impatient, I'm already impatient enough. Job Zot. In haci lady! I wish you all the best for your trip. Thank you very much for everything. Unfortunately, the various authorities didn't want us to see each other before your departure. Nevertheless, I will try to do fruitful work for you. 7. Uler Evening. Yours, Bob. I just received the approval for my plane ticket. It now depends on when I've paid. So I'll definitely be back with Pempteup. Yours, Rob.
